correctness.rationale: For gcd(b−1,n)=2, any multiple of n has even digit sum; one two-unit-digit multiple b^j+b^k allows concatenation of far-separated shifted copies to realize every positive even target. Strip each full nonunit prime-power factor of n; then large j cancels that part, and the remaining condition is a single b^t=−1 mod m. For odd prime powers the cyclic unit group gives the unique negative-one phase t≡order/2 mod order, compatible iff all v2(order)>0 coincide. The 2-primary factor e≥2 requires b=−1 mod2^e and all odd-component order valuations 1. CRT on unit/nonunit residue classes yields the printed products and sums. Independently enumerated 2734 eligible odd-b/even-n pairs (n≤120,b≤149) by modular power orbits and validated the closed all-base count for every even n≤200. This supports symbolic proof; arithmetic congruence argument supplies universality.
residual_risks: Finite checks bound n and b; full theorem relies on CRT/local unit group argument and digit concatenation without carries.
